name: JSI TRIGA Mark II, core 242 (58 elements) — OpenMC (M2)

provenance.model: sha256 of the 41 sweep case keys: a8d95a83c9aa77fdb52844c049787073901019c81b74795cbee9a3e07db7a21f
provenance.notes: Full-core OpenMC 0.15.3 transport at a uniform burnup (23.675258421961058 MWd/kg), 41 cases ({'particles': 20000, 'batches': 150, 'inactive': 50}). Transport results: reference state rho, rod worth curves, fuel and coolant temperature reactivity feedback, kinetics (beta_eff and Lambda by IFP), and fission power shapes (fraction of all fuel fission; the lowest axial bin holds fuel-follower fuel below the core, zero for regular elements, whose volume there is nominal; its relative uncertainty is the region total's). Base library inputs: thermal properties, poisons, plant instrumentation/trips/interlocks, delayed group lambdas, external source, rod scram profiles, and xenon table. Heat transfer: hA(dT) = h0 (dT / 100 K)^n with h0 = 1288.7 W/K and n = 0.2169, fitted to the measured power defect at 43.6 and 250 kW of the IAEA/JSI steady power ascension (one exercise, unknown core; docs/validation/m7-heat-transfer-results.md). It reproduces the held-out defect within 4 % and the shape of the fuel temperature rise within 0.03-0.05, but overshoots the defect at 2.9 kW (33-37 against 20.6 pcm). It is consistent with the measured hot-element temperature given a thermocouple peaking of 1.28 from the pulse database (docs/validation/m7-hot-element-2-results.md); the library's own shape arrays give a larger peaking.

calibration.reason: Uniform-burnup model (B246 = 23.675258421961058 MWd/kg) is not exactly critical at the measured critical rods; this offset makes the measured critical state critical. docs/validation/m2-burnup-results.md

interlocks.reason: The transient rod can only be fired in pulse mode.
Switching to pulse mode requires steady power below 1 kW.
